sm: Todd Friel opens by quoting the Puritan Thomas Brooks, who called ignorant, profane, and soul-flattering clergy the greatest plague that can befall a people, because without faithful preaching people perish. Friel says the Puritans also preached sweetly and comforted wounded believers, and he warns against swinging from cold, lofty preaching into a ditch of life-enhancement talks. He wants balance between declaring the word of the Lord and applying it. Drawing on an article from Cripplegate, he turns to John the Baptist, whom Jesus called the greatest man born of women. The first lesson is that John actually preached, proclaiming with authority rather than teaching information or sharing opinions. The second is that his preaching was biblical, explaining Old Testament law and prophecy rather than offering human thoughts.

Friel cites a British judge who said Genesis 1:27 is not compatible with human dignity, and a Seattle curriculum that asks students whether math is true. He argues these show a fight over authority, and that God, not people, determines what is true, right, and wrong. He says the prophets declared thus saith the Lord about seven hundred times. He then goes through more lessons from John the Baptist. His preaching focused on sin, called people to repent, warned of hell, told people how to be saved from judgment, and was loving. It also challenged listeners to examine themselves, called them to holiness, and focused on Christ. Friel then introduces Pastor Adam Tyson, a Master Seminary graduate from Los Angeles.

Friel says Tyson preached at a Kanye West Sunday service in Detroit and struck a good balance. In the clip, Tyson says God is not an out-of-touch grandpa or a sheriff out to catch people, but the same yesterday, today, and forever, a judge who is also merciful and loving. He says anyone who has really seen God will recognize three things. First, that God is holy, as in Isaiah chapter six, where the angels cry holy, holy, holy. Second, that we are sinners, as Isaiah said, woe is me. Third, that God forgives, as the burning coal touched Isaiah's lips. Tyson then calls believers to answer, here am I, Lord, send me, and to proclaim thus saith the Lord both forcefully and lovingly.
